summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 92.32% YoY to INR197.59 crore and PAT rose 87.89% to INR12.10 crore; management targets INR1,000 crore revenue by FY28.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest quarter, with consolidated revenue up 92.32% YoY to INR197.59 crore and EBITDA up 76.67% to INR20.14 crore. Sequentially, revenue grew about 20%, and EBITDA margin rose to 10.19% from 9.31% in Q3, helped by the Guwahati ramp-up from January 2026. For FY26, revenue rose 237.34% to INR607.75 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 9.66% from 14.24% and PAT margin to 5.76% from 6.11%, which management attributed to product mix. Management reiterated an INR1,000 crore revenue aspiration by FY28 and an internal 7% PAT margin target.

financial_highlights.metric: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue from operations
financial_highlights.change: +92.32% YoY (vs INR102.74 crore in Q4 FY25); about +20% QoQ

segments.name: FMCG and FMCG intermediates
segments.commentary: FMCG revenues crossed INR500 crore in FY26 and now form the majority of revenue. Intermediates are about 15% captively consumed and 85% sold to FMCG players such as ITC and Jyothy Labs; management expects 15-20% growth.

segments.name: Edible (spices and savouries)
segments.commentary: Started contributing meaningfully in FY26 from Bhilwara. Management expects about 20% growth in coming years and says FMCG will remain the largest contributor.

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Contributed around 20% of revenue in recent years; management expects it to fall to 10-12% at most. No demerger planned.

guidance_outlook: INR1,000 crore revenue targeted by FY28, described as a milestone rather than a final destination; management says it can be reached from existing capacity.
Organic growth of 10-15% a year, stated as over and above the roughly INR800 crore annualised run-rate.
Internal PAT margin target of about 7%; management said it would be nearly reached in FY27.
By FY28, target of INR1,000 crore revenue with a 1-1.5% improvement in existing EBITDA margins; operating leverage from higher utilisation is the main lever.
Inorganic growth: management is looking for FMCG acquisitions that offer good ROI, with no specifics given.
capex_capacity: Guwahati facility commissioned and revamped; ramp-up from January 2026 supports soap noodles and cosmetics for the Northeast and adjacent states (Bengal, Bihar).
Guwahati cosmetics capacity utilisation about 45-50%; Guwahati soap noodle capacity utilisation about 45-55%.
Management says there is no capacity constraint now and spare capacity exists in almost all categories, particularly personal care.
Management expects no major incremental capex in FY27-FY28; any spend would be small and aimed at aligning capacity.
Preferential issue proceeds: mostly used for edible manufacturing expansion and the Guwahati FMCG unit; about INR55 crore used for FMCG, about INR10 crore kept in FD, and the rest used for edible.
demand_pricing: Customer base of over 200; company says it grows mainly with existing customers and is adding new soap customers.
Manufactures for ITC, Godrej, Patanjali, Jyothy Laboratories and RCM among others; Swechha is a customer-owned brand.
Company is B2B only; B2C is a longer-term aim with partners, and no advertising is planned near term.
Competition described as regional; management sees no major competitive risk.
Raw material prices came under pressure at the end of Q4 FY26 and the start of Q1; supplies were not disrupted.
Debtor cycle described as stable and not increasing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the INR1,000 crore FY28 revenue target, and can it be met without new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the INR800 crore annualised run-rate from Q4 plus 10-15% organic growth and new soap customers, and said existing capacity is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA and PAT margins should be expected, and is 7% PAT reachable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the YoY margin decline to product mix, targets about 7% PAT, and said it will be nearly reached in FY27 with about 1-1.25% of operating leverage from higher utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the textile segment being demerged?
qa_highlights.answer: Textile is expected to fall from about 20% of revenue to 10-12% at most; no demerger is planned.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-15% organic growth conservative given the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management clarified that the 10-15% organic growth is over and above the INR800 crore base; acquisitions in FMCG will be considered if ROI is attractive.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Guwahati utilisation levels and raw material risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Cosmetics utilisation is about 45-50% and soap noodles about 45-55%; supplies were not disrupted despite raw material price pressure.

risks_watch: FY26 EBITDA and PAT margins declined YoY, and management has not shown the margin recovery path in numbers beyond the 7% PAT target.
Guwahati utilisation at about 45-55% leaves room for growth but also means the ramp is still in progress.
Raw material price pressure from the ongoing war noted at the end of Q4 FY26 and early Q1 FY27.
Textile share is falling, so FMCG and edible must carry growth; FMCG intermediates depend on a limited set of large FMCG customers.
Management indicated that the NSE listing depends on meeting conditions that have not yet been met.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and the FY28 target, with specific figures given on run-rate and margins. Less precise on inorganic plans, the NSE listing, and the 7% PAT timeline, where answers were brief and hedged ("nearby to the target"). Some answers during Q&A were unclear, and a few were corrected or restated by management.
key_quotes: Quarter 4 FY26 was our strongest quarter to date.
So this INR1,000 crores turnover can be achieved with the existing capacity and we don't see much of the expansion or investment in the capex side for achieving this INR1,000 crores topline.
We view this as an important milestone rather than the final destination.

growth.why: Management targets INR1,000 crore revenue by FY28 and 10-15% organic growth a year, backed mainly by existing spare capacity (Guwahati utilisation ~45-55%) and a customer base over 200, with no new capacity or specific order book numbers given; Q4 revenue grew 92% YoY.
